subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should Telegram first-run setup move to token-verified owner capture that writes dmPolicy="allowlist" and allowFrom, or should pairing remain the default with stronger manual allowlist setup?
rationale: This changes who can request or gain access to a bundled Telegram bot during first setup, and the safe answer depends on maintainer intent for usability, owner proof, and compatibility with existing pairing-mode operators.

options.title: Adopt verified owner capture
options.body: Fresh Telegram setup would display a short token, capture only a DM containing that token, and store the matching numeric sender ID under allowFrom with allowlist mode.

options.title: Keep pairing default with warnings
options.body: Leave pairing as the default and strengthen setup/docs warnings plus manual allowlist guidance for private bots.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap design
options.body: Treat this as one part of the broader one-line localhost plus Telegram bootstrap design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48471.

recommendation.title: Adopt verified owner capture
recommendation.body: Fresh Telegram setup would display a short token, capture only a DM containing that token, and store the matching numeric sender ID under allowFrom with allowlist mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Telegram setup, docs, config defaults, and security-default policy where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
